- Root: returned flood premium credit (customer's write).
- Hop F1 — **state-derived**: "A returned flood premium's kept amount is not settled until the annual flood premium on file has been reviewed against every flood insurance bill received since it was last set." -> reserve_flood_review_entry (`update_reserve_flood_ec384f8d`) found via "annual flood premium ... whenever the flood insurance bills on file are reviewed"; records show unreflected 2026-05-01 bills.
- Hop F2 — **state-derived**: same for hazard -> reserve_hazard_review_entry.
- Hop F3 — **state-derived**: "fixed only after the reserve's payment of the latest withdrawn hazard insurance term carries a refund credit" -> reserve ledger shows no refund credit on `34b61efb`; returned_hazard_premium_entry describes the write that posts "a refund credit that points at the reserve's original payment of the cancelled hazard term" (`return_hazard_premium_b6a621c2`, customer-side). The money must come from the customer -> ask about another insurer's refund.
- Hop H1/H2 — **state-derived**: returned_hazard_premium_entry clauses 3-4 wait on the same two reviews (already resolved by F1/F2).
- Order: {hazard review, flood review} -> hazard credit -> flood credit. No hop pre-solved: no flood document names a hazard tool or route; each hub names only its own tool.

### Counter-proofs
- "Only the flood refund": excluded by the F3 sentence plus the ledger (no refund credit on the latest withdrawn hazard payment) and by F1/F2 with unreflected bills; numerically the flood figure would be 1,415.89 instead of 1,406.46.
- Waiting/refusing the flood credit because no hazard refund is known: excluded because the caller can be asked and the hazard credit is a customer-side write she can make.
- Pro-rata unearned (baseline) vs short-rate / duplicate-coverage: excluded by the factor docs' tier conditions (cancellation date = paid replacement bill's due date).
- Relied-on bill ambiguity (residual risk, see section 3): "The review relies on the hazard insurance bill on file with the latest due date" read literally selects the received installment 2 (`7a8916b6`, due 2026-12-01), while the current-premium definition in the same document reads "the paid hazard insurance bill with the latest due date" (`d577d278`). I follow the literal relied-on sentence; a reader could pick the paid bill. Same for flood (`7da4ff2d` vs `d73cd96a`).
- Corporate-advance reading of `reserve_insurance` postings (retention 1 -> kept 2,808.00 / 1,415.89): excluded as in task 0.
